reason: Verification failed on critical, domain-level requirements. The current model is a generic one-time adoption framework and does not implement mask-specific daily behavior, entities, interactions, or required metrics/validations. With only three iterations remaining, a focused refactor can still align the simulation with the specification by introducing required classes and daily decision logic, aligning configuration keys, and computing spec-mandated metrics and validations.

specific_areas: Refactor to mask-specific daily behavior: Person with is_wearing_mask, mask_owned_count, fatigue dynamics; implement decide_wear_mask, purchase_mask, replace_mask, respond_to_policy.

Implement required entities and interactions: Retailer (inventory, price, restock, sell), PolicyAuthority (mandate, enforcement, fines, campaigns, supply coordination), Location (mask requirements); wire daily movement/attendance and enforcement.

Align configuration schema with spec keys and provide backward-compat mapping (population_size, network_topology=small_world, average_degree, mandate_day, enforcement, price_per_mask, mask_replacement_interval_days, purchase_threshold).

Compute required metrics and validations: adoption_rate_over_time (daily mask wearing), final_adoption_rate, time_to_threshold (70%), compliance_under_mandate, masks_sold_over_time, shortage_frequency, adoption_inequality_gini, policy_effect_lift, peak_adoption_rate, average_cost_per_person; add convergence_of_adoption and no_negative_inventory checks.
Series alignment and performance: append retailer_stockout_share daily even when supply disabled; cache a numpy RNG for Poisson restocking.

task_understanding.adjustments: Reframe the task explicitly as a mask adoption dynamics ABM with daily decisions, location context, policy enforcement, and retailer-level supply constraints; deprioritize generic information-propagation constructs that do not map to mask usage.

data_analysis.adjustments: Map config parameters from spec to internal keys; define baseline distributions for trust, risk, compliance, and income; plan grouping needed for inequality (income/demographics) and mandate window for lift computation.

model_planning.adjustments: Design class structure introducing Person, Retailer, PolicyAuthority, Location and a daily step order: restock -> movement/attendance -> policy enforcement -> social norm estimation -> decide_wear_mask -> purchase/replace -> update metrics; specify minimal interactions to satisfy required metrics.

code_generation.adjustments: Implement new classes and behaviors with docstrings; wire daily loop to update is_wearing_mask; add config mapping; collect required series under spec-compliant names; maintain main() direct call; ensure backward compatibility for legacy keys.

code_verification.adjustments: Add checks for presence of required classes and methods, series keys alignment, non-negative inventory across all retailers, and daily series length consistency; unit-test mandate effect, purchasing under shortage, and convergence validation.

simulation_execution.adjustments: Run short sanity simulations under: (a) no mandate/no supply constraints, (b) mandate active, (c) supply constraints with restocking; verify no runtime errors and that masks_sold_over_time and adoption_rate_over_time evolve plausibly.

result_evaluation.adjustments: Compute and return all spec metrics; ensure time_to_threshold logic returns -1 if not reached; compute policy_effect_lift with trend adjustment; average_cost_per_person from cumulative per-person spending.

feedback_generation.adjustments: Prioritize reporting on domain alignment milestones: presence of required entities, daily mask-wearing logic, spec-metric availability, and validation status; flag any deferred features and their impact explicitly.
